findings.title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser row exists
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (e.g. the user never visited/read the topic, the row was removed, or the topic was merged/moved), and line 107 immediately calls `tu.notification_level` on it. Any such request raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 to a user who just clicked an unsubscribe link in an email. The action needs to handle the nil case (create the record or go through `TopicUser.change`, which upserts).

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe exposed as a GET with no CSRF protection
findings.body: `unsubscribe` is routed as `GET t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and mutates `TopicUser.notification_level`, and `check_xhr` is skipped for it. Because Rails does not verify CSRF tokens for GET requests, any third-party page can trigger it for a logged-in user with e.g. ``, silently muting topics. Link-prefetching/scanning agents that carry the user's session (browser prefetch, some security proxies) can also fire it unintentionally. The mutation should happen on a POST/PUT (or be protected by a signed one-time key, like the existing digest unsubscribe key flow).

findings.title: Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping and MessageBus notification
findings.body: The new action writes `notification_level` directly on the record instead of using `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`. As a result `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` are not updated (the level stays attributed to the old reason, e.g. `auto_watch_category`) and no `/topic/:id` MessageBus `notification_level_change` message is published, so other open tabs/clients keep showing the stale notification level and auto-tracking logic sees an inconsistent reason id.

findings.title: Unsubscribe link requires an active session
findings.body: `:unsubscribe` was added to the `ensure_logged_in` before_filter, so a recipient who clicks the per-topic unsubscribe link from an email while not logged in (the common case for mail clients in a different browser/profile) gets a not-logged-in error/login redirect instead of unsubscribing. Email unsubscribe flows in this codebase otherwise use a token (see `email/unsubscribe/:key`); the new link should either use such a key or at least redirect back to this URL after login.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url} and will raise for callers that don't pass it
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` string gained a `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation, but `Email::MessageBuilder` provides no default for it (only `site_name`, `base_url`, `user_preferences_url` are defaulted). Any `build_email` call that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` in `MessageBuilder#body`/`#html_part`, breaking email delivery. The need to update `message_builder_spec.rb` to add `unsubscribe_url` demonstrates this. Add a fallback in `MessageBuilder` (e.g. default `unsubscribe_url` to the user preferences URL) so existing/plugin callers keep working.

findings.title: Unsubscribe page text claims notifications stop even when level is only lowered to regular
findings.body: `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` reads "You will stop receiving notifications for <title>", but the server action lowers a watching/tracking user to `regular` (not `muted`) on the first click. At `regular` the user still receives notifications/emails for replies, mentions and quotes, so the message is wrong for the most common case and users will believe they are unsubscribed when they are not. Either mute on the first click or make the text reflect the actual resulting level.

findings.title: No specs for the new unsubscribe action
findings.body: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` endpoint has no request/controller spec. Untested behaviours that are easy to get wrong and are currently broken or risky: missing `TopicUser` row (raises NoMethodError), the watching/tracking -> regular vs regular/muted -> muted transition, the 301 redirect when the slug is absent or mismatched, and the anonymous-user path. Please add specs covering these.

findings.title: Route name topicUnsubscribe may not resolve the template at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs
findings.body: The route is registered as `topicUnsubscribe`, while the template was added at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` (i.e. template name `topic/unsubscribe`) and the view at `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` (name `topic-unsubscribe`). The resolver decamelizes/dasherizes route names, so `topicUnsubscribe` looks for `topic_unsubscribe`/`topic-unsubscribe`; the template and view names are therefore inconsistent with each other, and the unsubscribe page risks rendering blank. Please make the names consistent (e.g. put the template at `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`) or add an explicit `renderTemplate`.
